title: 美国情报：不再可靠，前军情六处首长说透
speaker: John Sawers

segments.en: It is a fragmented world and more and more countries are wanting more intelligence. Case in point, Japan.
segments.zh: 这是一个碎片化的世界，越来越多的国家想要更多情报。日本就是例子。

segments.en: It wants to form what is similar to the CIA. What do you make of that?
segments.zh: 它想组建类似CIA的机构。你怎么看？

segments.en: Well, I think two things are happening. First of all, the threat to countries like Japan and also to European countries like Germany has gone up.
segments.zh: 我认为有两件事在发生。首先，日本和德国等欧洲国家面临的威胁上升了。

segments.en: So you need better intelligence on the threats that you're facing and not just the capability of your opponents but what they're intending to do as the key bit of intelligence is intent.
segments.zh: 所以你需要更好的情报来应对威胁，不仅是对手的能力，还有他们的意图，因为情报的关键是意图。

segments.en: And at the same time, the Americans have become a less reliable partner in intelligence sharing and so you have to be more self-sufficient.
segments.zh: 同时，美国在情报共享上变得不那么可靠，所以你必须更加自给自足。

segments.en: So I'm not surprised and I welcome moves by Japan, by Germany and other countries which don't have a long tradition of providing more than effective skilled intelligence.
segments.zh: 所以我不意外，也欢迎日本、德国等没有长期提供高效情报传统的国家采取行动。

segments.en: So it is realistic. How long do you think it would take for Japan to get there?
segments.zh: 所以这是现实的。你认为日本需要多久才能达到？

segments.en: Well, it has taken us a hundred years to get MI6 to where it is. So these things do not happen overnight.
segments.zh: 我们花了100年才让军情六处达到今天的位置。所以这些事不是一夜之间发生的。

segments.en: You have to build up a culture, you have to build up an expertise within the organization.
segments.zh: 你必须在组织内建立一种文化，建立专业知识。

segments.en: You have to have the technology which enables you to run secret agents in a world of very great surveillance.
segments.zh: 你必须有技术，能在高度监控的世界里运行秘密特工。

segments.en: So I think the Japanese will need some help there reaching out to other partners like ourselves to provide that assistance.
segments.zh: 所以我认为日本在这方面需要一些帮助，向像我们这样的伙伴寻求协助。

segments.en: But you have to start somewhere and I think now is a good time for Japan, Germany and others to move out of the post-World War II mindset that you don't build up offensive intelligence services and you rely on your partners to provide you with the intelligence you need.
segments.zh: 但你必须从某处开始，我认为现在是日本、德国等国摆脱二战后思维的好时机——那种不建立进攻性情报机构、依赖伙伴提供所需情报的思维。

segments.en: We're moving on from that world now and one big component of it is the United States has become America first is not prioritizing the needs of its allies.
segments.zh: 我们正在离开那个世界，一个大的因素是美国的“美国优先”不再优先考虑盟友的需求。
